transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-12
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Recording ID: ff-20251112-0457
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Torres (BlueHarbor - Procurement), Daniel Wu (BlueHarbor - Legal), Priya Nair (BlueHarbor - Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
- High-level procurement gate: customer needs clarified DPA and a few MSA exceptions re: data residency and KMS. Pricing escalation requires procurement committee sign-off; customer wants Redwoods committed SLA for percent p99 and audit logs. SE to run bench on dev dataset; AE to share redline and pricing spreadsheet.

Topics: MSA exceptions, DPA terms, SLA levels, pricing approval path, pilot topology (dedicated vs private), KMS/SSO and audit log requirements.

Action items (parsed): see metadata section - list sent to CRM.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery Chen: All right, thanks everyone for jumping on. I think we said 45 minutes, so we'll try to be crisp. This is Avery from Redwood, AE on the account, and Samir our solutions engineer is here. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Maya Torres: Doing well, thanks. Busy week but we need to nail the legal items so, appreciate the time.
[00:18] Daniel Wu: Hi, Daniel here. I'll mostly be covering our DPA/MSA redlines but Priya will cover the technical constraints.
[00:24] Priya Nair: Hey all. Yup, I'll jump in on network and encryption questions.
[00:30] Samir Rao: Great. Quick agenda — clarify the MSA exceptions you sent, walk DPA items (data residency, KMS), discuss SLA and uptime targets, and then pricing approval path. We'll finish with explicit next steps. Sound ok?
[00:43] Maya: Sounds good.
[00:44] Daniel: Yep.

[02:05] Maya: I'll start — procurement wants to make sure we understand the gate. We have a vendor review next Tuesday. For us to make it to the committee we need the DPA settled and a clear view on whether Redwood can meet our residency requirements and KMS controls. Also pricing needs the total committed spend number.
[02:28] Avery: Totally understood. On residency — Redwood offers hosted (multi-tenant), dedicated, and private (VPC/on-prem) — so we can map to your requirement. Can you remind me which data sets you consider restricted? Is it PHI or de-identified?
[02:44] Priya: It's mostly PHI plus some patient contact metadata. So effectively HIPAA-restricted. We need the DPA to reflect that and KMS integration because keys must be customer-managed.
[03:00] Samir: Understood — we do have a Private deployment option where you can bring your key via KMS/HSM and we can isolate compute in your VPC. There are tradeoffs though: latency and cost tend to be higher for fully private on-prem deployments versus Redwood Dedicated in our cloud region with customer KMS.
[03:22] Daniel: That's an important tradeoff. Our legal team will likely prefer the highest control but procurement will push back on cost. We need options and numbers.

[05:20] Avery: Ok, on the MSA exceptions you highlighted — I pulled the document — you called out indemnity caps, data residency carve-outs, and audit rights. Can we go line-by-line on those three?
[05:32] Daniel: Sure. On indemnity: we can't accept unlimited third-party claims related to data exposures, so we proposed a capped liability tied to a 12-month spend. In the DPA we also want explicit cross-border transfer language and a statement that logs can be exported for audits.
[05:48] Samir: When you say logs, do you mean token-level audit logs or higher-level request traces? Our platform can emit detailed audit logs, but token-level export often intersects with retention policy. We usually default to short retention on hosted by default but can extend for Dedicated/Private.
[06:05] Priya: We need per-request audit trails with request/response hashes and timestamps for 12 months. We also need the ability to run audits on-prem if necessary.
[06:18] Avery: Right. So operationally we can surface request-level logs to your SIEM via syslog/forwarder from Dedicated or Private. For hosted we'd need an add-on. We'll note that in the redline.

[08:50] Maya: Pricing — our procurement team flagged that the pricing sheet has a tier for Dedicated that was notably higher than we expected. Can you speak to discounts for committed usage and how pricing approvals flow?
[09:06] Avery: Yes. Typically we offer committed-reserved discounts for 12/24 month contracts. There's also volume tiers — once you hit X tokens/month we can tier. For procurements we usually provide a pricing spreadsheet with committed spend scenarios and an approver signature block.
[09:24] Daniel: But procurement also needs a path: if the commit gets escalated we need a price anchoring memo that says why Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private makes sense for our use-case. That memo helps the committee approve the spend.
[09:40] Samir: We can provide a short doc: recommended deployment (e.g., start Hosted for dev, Dedicated for production), expected per-token cost numbers, projected monthly spend for 6/12/24 month commits, and a risk table for degradation/fallback. I can produce a bench run on a dev dataset to show latency/cost tradeoffs.
[09:56] Priya: That bench will be useful. Also include quantization/precision options we discussed — it impacts cost and model fidelity which our clinical team will care about.

[12:05] Daniel: Back to the DPA — one of our compliance requirements is that keys must be customer-controlled, FIPS 140-2/HSM-backed. Also we require contractual language that Redwood will not access customer plaintext except for processing and as required by law.
[12:24] Samir: Our KMS integrations support both cloud KMSs and customer HSM via bring-your-own-key for Private. For Dedicated we can integrate customer KMS in our cloud region; the keys remain under your control and we have key-wrapping flow. I will note the FIPS requirement and map to our security docs.
[12:42] Priya: And minimum encryption in transit and at rest — TLS 1.2+ and AES-256.
[12:48] Avery: Yep, standard. We'll reference SOC 2 and provide audit artifact flow.

[15:30] Maya: On the MSA indemnity cap, procurement historically expects cap equal to 12 months of contract value or a fixed multiple. Is Redwood open to that?
[15:42] Avery: We are typically open to a 12-month cap for commercial customers, subject to review. For enterprise deals we can negotiate. I'll mark that as a cliff note but it's reasonable.
[15:52] Daniel: We'll propose 12-months; legal may push for exceptions on willful misconduct.

[18:25] Samir: A question from the engineering side — Priya, could you confirm network constraints? Are you expecting us to connect into your VPC, or do you prefer egress controls with IP allowlist?
[18:36] Priya: We prefer VPC peering or PrivateLink for production. For dev it's ok to use IP allowlists. Also, firewall egress is locked so we may need to handle NAT and endpoint routing.
[18:50] Samir: Ok, that argues for Dedicated or Private for production. We'll sketch topology options: Dedicated with VPC peering + customer-managed KMS, and Private on-prem with direct HSM integration.

[21:05] Maya: Another procurement point — we need a statement of SLA, specifically p99 latency and availability SLA with credits. Can you commit to an SLA?
[21:16] Avery: We offer SLA-backed uptime targets for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have a best-effort SLO but not the same commercial SLA. Can you state the minimum availability and p99 you need?
[21:28] Daniel: We're asking for 99.9% availability and p99 under 400ms for inference for our latency-sensitive flows. Is that realistic?
[21:38] Samir: 400ms p99 is aggressive, depends on model size and sequence length. For smaller seq lengths and quantized models, Dedicated can get close, maybe p99 in 200-500ms on optimized kernels. For large-context generative models p99 will be higher. We'll include model-specific numbers in the bench.
[21:55] Priya: We mostly will use a 2k token cap for now on clinical summarization — that tends to drive up p99. We'll need fallback routing to a smaller model for spikes.
[22:08] Avery: We can add an automatic fallback policy to the deployment config — route to a cheaper smaller model if latency spikes or capacity is constrained; that helps keep the app online and reduce costs. We'll document that in the runbook.

[25:40] Maya: On procurement workflow — approvals need a legal statement on data residency and an insurance certificate. Can you provide cyber insurance proof?
[25:52] Avery: Yes, we can provide our current cyber insurance cert and add it to the vendor package. I'll attach the cert.
[25:58] Daniel: Also, we need to ensure the DPA references EU standard contractual clauses where applicable. We want explicit cross-border clauses.
[26:10] Samir: Noted. We'll ask our legal to include SCC references in the DPA redline for EU data.

[28:40] Priya: One thing that's tricky — the pilot environment must not touch production PHI. We need a masked or synthetic dataset for the bench. Samir, can you confirm you'll run on a synthetic dev set?
[28:52] Samir: Yes, we'll run on a seeded synthetic dataset that mirrors token distribution and sequence length. We'll share the config and the runner script.

[31:05] Maya: Procurement will also want to know whether Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for accounts. That's a gating item for onboarding.
[31:18] Avery: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning in the Console. For Private installs we can integrate with your IdP directly. We'll include the SSO + SCIM configuration doc.
[31:30] Daniel: Good. Also need role-based access controls for audit separation — we don't want devs accessing billing keys.
[31:38] Samir: RBAC is supported — we can separate roles for billing, dev, and ops and limit key export.

[33:55] Maya: What is the legal turnaround you can commit for redline review once we send the DPA comments? We usually need a two-way track so we can bring it to committee.
[34:06] Avery: Our legal normally turns around initial redline within 3-5 business days for standard items, longer if there are novel exceptions. Given this is an enterprise-ish ask with KMS/HSM, I would plan for 5 business days to be conservative.
[34:18] Daniel: Ok that works as long as we get a draft before the procurement committee date.

[36:10] Priya: One more technical ask — can Redwood guarantee that models will not log request payloads to support RPO? We need clear retention and also the ability to purge data on termination.
[36:23] Samir: We have retention controls per deployment. For Dedicated/Private we can set retention to your policy and support purge APIs on contract termination. We'll add contractual language that we won't retain customer data beyond the agreed retention window.
[36:36] Priya: Great.

[38:50] Maya: Ok, let's talk next steps — procurement will need the redlined MSA and pricing sheet by Friday so this can be reviewed internally. We'll also expect the security artifact bundle.
[39:01] Avery: I'll send the redline and pricing spreadsheet by Friday EOD PT. Samir will run the bench and send a short results sheet by Wednesday. We'll also attach SOC 2 attestation and cyber insurance.
[39:12] Daniel: We'll circulate DPA comments within our legal and get them back by 2025-11-19. If there are big issues we'll request an earlier legal-only sync.

[41:05] Samir: Quick note on bench methodology — we'll run a 24-hour synthetic run to capture p50/p90/p99 and cost per token with batching/quantization variations. We'll also include a sample config for Dedicated vs Private.
[41:18] Priya: Please include memory and GPU-type assumptions; those impact latency.
[41:24] Samir: Will do — I'll include instance types and kernel selection notes.

[43:00] Maya: Sounds like we're aligned. Any competitors in play from your side? We've seen some benchmarking from Anthropic and a short evaluation from OpenAI endpoints.
[43:12] Avery: We're familiar; we'll include a short comparison note but won't go into marketing claims. The key is operational fit: KMS, residency, and SLA.
[43:24] Daniel: Great.

[45:00] Avery: All right, thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the redline and pricing doc. Samir will post the bench link and config. Maya/Daniel you'll circulate internal comments and we will reconvene if legal needs.
[45:14] Maya: Thanks.
[45:16] Daniel: Thanks all.
[45:18] Priya: Thanks.

End of recording.

Notes on transcription quality: medium — occasional mis-hears around technical acronyms and kernel names, speaker boundaries occasionally approximate.
